raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59185.

On two B200 nodes without a multi-node NVLink (MNNVL) fabric, a TP=4 group with two GPUs per node can hang during communicator initialization and fail at the 1,800-second Gloo timeout. `SymmMemCommunicator` currently enters symmetric-memory rendezvous without checking whether the topology supports cross-node memory handles. An error on some ranks can leave other ranks blocked, so catching `RuntimeError` alone does not provide a safe fallback.

This change checks locality before allocating symmetric memory. Single-node groups retain the existing path; cross-node groups enter rendezvous only if every rank reports fabric support. The fabric probe returns false when unavailable or unsuccessful. CustomAllreduce's existing group-wide MNNVL gate also requires fabric support, since local multicast capability alone is insufficient.

The branch is based on upstream `main` at `3e2a7e74a556623ddee3a327299d7bf04055501e`. The previously tested patch was adapted to retain main's `_all_ranks_true` helper. Regression tests extend the existing distributed suites to cover non-fabric groups, partial fabric support, supported groups, and avoiding allocation/rendezvous when disabled.

Duplicate-work check on September 29, 2026: issue #59185 had no comments or open PR referencing it. An open-PR search for `SymmMemCommunicator fabric` returned #41834, which concerns DeepSeek V4 support on SM12x and does not modify the three communicator files changed here. The merged #53253 added CustomAllreduce gating but did not guard the separate `SymmMemCommunicator` rendezvous.

AI assistance was used to prepare this change and description (OpenAI Codex), building on an internal recorded experiments.

## Test Plan

Re-run the two-node B200 reproduction from #59185 against the unmodified base and this branch using the same pinned software and workload configuration. Verify that TP=4 (two GPUs per node) starts and completes model evaluation, and retain the TP=2 control (one GPU per node). Also exercise single-node and MNNVL-connected configurations; the prior experiment did not cover those paths.

The change adds one same-node probe during SymmMemCommunicator construction and one CPU MIN all-reduce for cross-node groups. Check startup behavior on supported topologies as well as fallback on unsupported ones. An unavailable FlashInfer fabric probe conservatively disables cross-node symmetric-memory fast paths.

## Test Result

| Configuration | Unmodified vLLM | Combined candidate |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, TP=4, two nodes × two B200 GPUs | Startup fails; workload ends after ~1,921 s, including the 1,800-second Gloo timeout | Startup and GSM8K 10% subset evaluation complete in ~455 s; accuracy 0.4545 |
| Nemotron Super V3 120B-A12B FP8, TP=2, two nodes × one B200 GPU | Completes; GSM8K subset accuracy 0.9697 | Completes; accuracy 0.9394 |

Those experiments used vLLM `0.29.1rc1.dev573+ge97573215` and the same upstream base digest, `sha256:f75fec992c293dd41042745f8aa71bfdf12b188b6a01e0baf075e4bca5d297e5`, with separate node allocations. They tested both communicator changes together, once per arm and configuration, and measured total workload time rather than startup latency. The evaluation subset had 132 questions and no pass threshold; the TP=2 score difference is four questions. These results support the candidate's startup fix but do not establish accuracy equivalence, isolate either change, or validate this rebase. Single-node, MNNVL, TP=8, and NVFP4 coverage remain outstanding.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [x] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.

No new model, API, or configuration option is introduced; no documentation update is proposed.

</details>

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(

+        (True, False, False, True),

+    monkeypatch, same_node, local_fabric, peer_fabric, enabled
+):
+    """Never enter potentially blocking rendezvous without support on all ranks."""
+    group = SimpleNamespace(group_name="test")
+    backend = SimpleNamespace(

+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(symm_mem, "has_mnnvl_fabric_support", fabric_probe)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(envs, "VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", False)
+
+    def agree_on_fabric(support, *, op, group):
+        assert op == dist.ReduceOp.MIN
+        assert support.device.type == "cpu"
+        if not peer_fabric:
+            support.zero_()
+
+    agreement = Mock(side_effect=agree_on_fabric)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(symm_mem.dist, "all_reduce", agreement)
+    communicator = symm_mem.SymmMemCommunicator(group, "cuda:0", max_size_override=2)
+
+    assert communicator.disabled is not enabled
+    assert backend.empty.call_count == int(enabled)
+    assert backend.rendezvous.call_count == int(enabled)
+    assert fabric_probe.call_count == int(not same_node)
+    assert agreement.call_count == int(not same_node)
+

 def symm_mem_allreduce_worker(local_rank: int, world_size: int, q: mp.Queue):

     return world_size > NCCL_SYMM_MEM_ALL_REDUCE_CONFIG["always_use_above_world_size"]
 
 
+def has_mnnvl_fabric_support(device_index: int) -> bool:
+    """Return whether this GPU is attached to a multi-node NVLink fabric.
+
+    Without fabric memory handles, torch symmetric memory exchanges buffers as
+    POSIX file descriptors over node-local Unix domain sockets, so it can only
+    rendezvous ranks that share a host. This probe is collective-free and
+    conservative: it reports ``False`` whenever FlashInfer's fabric probe
+    cannot run, which only disables a cross-node fast path.
+    """
+    try:
+        from flashinfer.comm.mnnvl import is_mnnvl_fabric_supported
+
+        return bool(is_mnnvl_fabric_supported(device_index))
+    except Exception as error:
+        logger.debug("MNNVL fabric probe failed: %s", error)
+        return False
+

     AllGather / ReduceScatter collectives."""

     CUSTOM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES,
     gpu_p2p_access_check,
+    has_mnnvl_fabric_support,
 )
 from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import in_the_same_node_as
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
@@ -68,17 +69,17 @@ def _group_can_attempt_mnnvl(
 ) -> bool:
     """Return whether every rank can enter the cross-node MNNVL path.
 
-    MNNVL is available only on Blackwell-class GPUs. Local multicast support
-    is necessary but does not establish that the process group spans an MNNVL
-    domain; the symmetric-memory rendezvous below performs that group-level
-    check. The CPU all-reduce keeps every rank on the same control-flow path
-    when a heterogeneous or partially configured group is encountered.
+    Local multicast support does not imply an inter-node NVLink fabric.
+    Without fabric handles, a cross-node symmetric-memory rendezvous can hang
+    instead of failing on all ranks. Require fabric support on every rank
+    before attempting rendezvous, which still checks for a shared MNNVL domain.
     """
     device_index = device.index
     local_support = (
         device_index is not None
         and current_platform.has_device_capability(100, device_index)
         and _has_local_multicast_support(device)
+        and has_mnnvl_fabric_support(device_index)
     )
     return _all_ranks_true(group, local_support)

@@ -8,7 +8,9 @@
 import vllm.envs as envs
 from vllm.distributed.device_communicators.all_reduce_utils import (
     SYMM_MEM_ALL_REDUCE_MAX_SIZES,
+    has_mnnvl_fabric_support,
 )
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import in_the_same_node_as
 from vllm.logger import init_logger
 from vllm.platforms import current_platform
 
@@ -77,6 +79,13 @@ def __init__(
                 self.world_size,
             )
             return
+        if not self._group_can_rendezvous():
+            logger.info_once(
+                "SymmMemCommunicator: the process group spans nodes that are "
+                "not connected by a multi-node NVLink fabric, communicator is "
+                "not available."
+            )
+            return
         # Use override max_size if provided, otherwise use default
         if max_size_override is not None:
             self.max_size = max_size_override
@@ -114,6 +123,30 @@ def __init__(
         if envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT:
             self.disabled = True
 
+    def _group_can_rendezvous(self) -> bool:
+        """Return whether a symmetric-memory rendezvous on the group can finish.
+
+        Unless fabric memory handles are available, torch passes each rank's
+        buffer as a POSIX file descriptor to the next rank in a ring, over a
+        node-local Unix domain socket. On a group that spans nodes, a rank whose
+        successor is on another node fails to connect, while a rank whose
+        successor is local but whose predecessor is on another node waits for a
+        descriptor that never arrives. The rendezvous then hangs on some ranks
+        instead of failing on all of them, and the ranks that continue time out
+        in their next collective. Every rank of the group reaches this check,
+        so it decides collectively before allocating and all ranks take the
+        same branch.
+        """
+        if all(in_the_same_node_as(self.group, source_rank=0)):
+            return True
+        fabric_support = torch.tensor(
+            int(has_mnnvl_fabric_support(torch.accelerator.current_device_index())),
+            dtype=torch.int32,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+        dist.all_reduce(fabric_support, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN, group=self.group)
+        return bool(fabric_support.item())
+
     def should_use_symm_mem(self, inp: torch.Tensor):
         if self.disabled:
             return False
